chunks: From him, from Musa ibn Ja'far al-Baghdadi, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abdullah, from Wasil ibn Sulayman, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) had a close companion (khalit) during the pre-Islamic period. When he was sent (as a prophet), his companion met him and said to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), 'May Allah reward you with goodness as a companion, for you used to agree and not argue.' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'And you, may Allah reward you with goodness as a companion, for you never rejected a profit nor did you withhold your teeth (i.e., show harshness or stinginess).'

key_terms.ضِرْساً: Tooth / molar (metaphorically for harshness or stinginess)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say to his pre-Islamic companion regarding their relationship?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) consistent moral character, demonstrating that his gentleness and lack of contentiousness were inherent traits even before prophethood. The companion’s specific praise of the Prophet’s 'non-argumentative' nature underscores the Islamic ideal of *hilm* (forbearance), while the reciprocal praise for the companion’s generosity in trade reflects the continuity of virtuous social conduct from the pre-Islamic period into the Islamic era.
